clue.text: Obstructed editors going after troublemaker

indicators.note: going after tells us the editors come behind the troublemaker in the answer

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil, a troublemaker
ED is the standard abbreviation for an editor, so two editors give ED twice

explanation.surface: Staff on a newspaper are hampered by some mischief-maker who chases them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impeded is to be hindered or held back, a plain synonym of obstructed.

clue.text: Consume minute fish that is put outside

indicators.note: put outside says the that-is letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: IE stands for id est, Latin for that is
the bib is a small fish of the cod family, also called pouting

explanation.surface: Eat a tiny fish that has been left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink or take in, so it means to consume.

clue.text: Queen holding up one drink or another

indicators.note: in a down clue the queen is underneath, holding up the drink

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Her Majesty props up one drink or another at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one drink or another' reads as any drink, but PORT is one drink and the answer, a dark beer, is another.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is a dark beer, so it is a further drink beside the port.

clue.text: Whisky, for instance, I even now put in fruit

indicators.note: put in tells us the pieces go inside the fruit

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm
taken as written
still means even now, as in it is still raining

explanation.surface: Someone puts whisky into a fruit dessert, even now.
explanation.walkthrough: A still is also the apparatus for making whisky, adding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a liquid produced by distilling, an example of the product.

clue.text: Partner speaking slangily in European language

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old ...' means one's wife, from duchess
the language spoken in the Netherlands

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' as wife is London Cockney slang, short for duchess.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of the Netherlands, and Cockney slang for a man's wife.

clue.text: House records for believers in complex systems

parts.note: lists are written records of items

explanation.surface: A house keeps documents for people who think in terms of whole systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Holism is the belief that complex systems must be understood as wholes, so its adherents are believers in complex systems.

clue.text: A lot of grim vexation about university lecturer who's aggressive?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its end is dropped

parts.note: hard can mean grim, as in hard times

indicators.note: about means the vexation surrounds the university letter

parts.note: anger is vexation or annoyance

explanation.surface: An angry academic delivers a grim talk in a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts the last letter from HARD to give HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who harangues gives a long, forceful lecture, so is an aggressive lecturer.

clue.text: Provides accommodation and reasons for reserving?

definitions.meaning: rents out rooms or property to tenants
in tennis a let is called when a serve must be replayed, so it is a reason for serving again

explanation.walkthrough: 'reserving' reads as booking, but it splits as re-serving, serving again in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord rents out rooms, and in tennis a let means the serve is retaken.

clue.text: Part of a reckoning, but a lot's going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant's sum is partly worked out but much of it is in error.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial sum within a larger calculation is one piece of an account.

clue.text: Most pleasant minute in second trial

indicators.note: in says the tiny piece sits inside the other two

parts.note: a test is a trial
wee is Scottish for small, so minute

explanation.surface: A lovely moment in a court case being retried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the adjective meaning tiny (my-NOOT), not the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetest is the superlative of sweet, meaning the most pleasing or agreeable.

clue.text: Attempts to capture queen and rooks, perhaps

indicators.note: to capture means the attempts surround and hold the queen's letter

parts.note: bids are attempts, as in a bid for power
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess player tries to take the opponent's queen and rooks.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'rooks' look like chess pieces, but here they are the crow-like birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks are an example of the feathered creatures, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Record supporter during play, having run wildly into disorderly battle

indicators.note: into says the first rearranged piece goes inside the second
disorderly signals the letters of battle are jumbled
running wildly suggests the letters of run are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical performance where an actor dashes madly into a chaotic stage fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' looks like a verb or a sporting best, but the definition is a whole phrase for the deck a disc spins on while being played.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record sits on the rotating deck of a player while it is being played.

clue.text: Spotting part of problem is hinge

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Noticing that the trouble lies with a door's hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting here means marking with spots or stains, which is what marring with blemishes does.

clue.text: Thing of little value — copy many answers here without a break

definitions.meaning: an old Dutch coin of tiny worth, hence anything trivial

definitions.text: copy many answers here without a break
definitions.meaning: the theme song says birds, bees and others all do this, so copying them means doing the same, written as one word

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is the Cole Porter song in which birds, bees and even the Letts and Lithuanians are said to 'do it'; many grid answers are among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A doit was a small Dutch coin, so the word came to mean a trifle or something worthless.

clue.text: Not appreciating multinational group taking a lot of fuel around hospital

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: around says the fuel surrounds the hospital letter

parts.note: a full fuel tank holds a lot of fuel

explanation.surface: The United Nations ships in lots of fuel to a hospital and gets no thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ungrateful fails to show thanks, so does not appreciate what was done.

clue.text: Comic annual is hit for some Europeans

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters are played about with for comic effect

explanation.surface: A funny yearly publication proves a success with readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic annual' reads as a children's yearbook, but 'Comic' is the signal to rearrange ANNUAL IS HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of the Baltic state between Latvia and Poland are a group of people from Europe.

clue.text: Ways of treating broken heart with culinary treats

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: pies are baked treats

explanation.surface: A heartbroken person seeks comfort in food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken heart' reads as grief, but 'broken' rearranges HEART into THERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapies are courses of medical or psychological treatment.

clue.text: Learned gold coin in river turned up

indicators.note: in says the coin sits inside the river
turned up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
a ducat was a gold coin used across Europe

explanation.surface: An old coin is found in a river by someone well versed in history.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is well educated, schooled and knowledgeable; this is an adjective sense.

clue.text: Centuries for MCC, for example

parts.note: MCC is 1200 in Roman numerals and a century is a hundred, one part in twelve of that total

explanation.walkthrough: MCC is also the Marylebone Cricket Club, the body behind English cricket, so 'centuries' looks like a batsman's hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred divided into twelve hundred gives one part of twelve equal parts.

clue.text: Practical, as one is prone to be, facing garden?

definitions.meaning: sensible and realistic, not head in the clouds

definitions.text: as one is prone to be, facing garden?
definitions.meaning: someone lying prone faces the ground, literally face down towards the soil

explanation.definitionFit: Someone sensible and unpretentious is described with this idiom, the opposite of having one's head in the clouds.

clue.text: Stick together with male in centre

indicators.note: in says the male goes inside the centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man in the middle of things keeps a group together.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together firmly or be united.

clue.text: County with indefinable quality in which one may live

parts.note: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
it is that special something, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A rural county has a certain charm for those who reside there.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room rented flat is a place a person can make a home.

clue.text: General name for group of plants as fuel, we hear

definitions.text: General name for group of plants

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: coal is a fuel burnt in fires

explanation.surface: Gardeners discuss a catch-all name for some plants that might be burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole is also a nod to Cole Porter, writer of the theme song.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is the collective term for brassicas such as cabbage and kale.

clue.text: What young man may do in spring or autumn with current novel's revision

definitions.text: What young man may do in spring

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: revision means the novel is rewritten, its letters reordered

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A romantic writer revises a book through the seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson wrote that in spring a young man's fancy turns to thoughts of love; 'revision' rearranges NOVEL into NLOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial young man becomes smitten in springtime, the season of romance.

clue.text: Neighbours of 14 or 6, say

definitions.note: the Europeans of 14 across live next to Latvia

indicators.note: say signals the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the answer to 6 down, a word for rents out

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue about people living next door to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvians border Lithuania, so they are the neighbours of the Baltic people at 14.

clue.text: Busy people in great musical trio, so-called

indicators.note: so-called means the letter names are spoken, giving the word as said

parts.note: the three Bs of music are Bach, Beethoven and Brahms

explanation.surface: Hard-working people in a famous band of three, as they are known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great musical trio' suggests a band; it is the three Bs of classical music.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy workers are proverbially compared to the buzzing insects of a hive.

clue.text: Sign pointing towards hotel not on? Absolutely

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letters of the word on

parts.note: a direction sign might read 'To the Hilton', the hotel chain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller follows a hotel signpost and finds it says the wrong thing, emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something up to the handle of a sword means fully, so it is an idiom for completely.

clue.text: Soundly beats it as a source of irritation

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to beat it is slang for to run away

explanation.surface: Someone is given a good thrashing, which causes annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly beats' looks like a thorough thrashing; 'beats it' is the slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: These biting parasitic insects are a classic cause of itching and irritation.

clue.text: Stops some who believe in creator taking son in

indicators.note: taking with in means the believers hold the son inside them
in completes taking ... in, the believers surrounding the son

parts.note: deists believe in a creator god who does not intervene
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogy

explanation.surface: Believers in a creator stop when one of them adopts a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a synonym for halts.

clue.text: Foreigner occupying street, striking

indicators.note: occupying means the foreigner sits inside the street

parts.note: an alien is a foreign national

explanation.surface: Picture an immigrant squatting on a road during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is one that stands out, prominent and noticeable.
